subtitle: When the River Road to Bengal Opened

panels.shot: wide, split-composition tableau showing two armies poised on either bank of a marshy field near waterways, Munim Khan on an elephant at left, Daud Khan Karrani on horseback at right
panels.action: Munim Khan and Daud Khan Karrani face each other from opposite sides of a misty battlefield near river channels, war-camps stretching behind them under a brooding Bengal sky.

dialogue.text: In 1575, at Tukaroi, an aging Mughal general and a young Afghan sultan cut a treaty that seemed to save Daud Khan—yet it opened Bengal’s gates to Akbar.

i18n.hi: १५७५ में तुकड़ई पर, एक बूढ़ा मुग़ल सेनापति और एक नौजवान अफ़ग़ान सुल्तान ने ऐसा समझौता किया, जिसने दाऊद ख़ाँ को बचा लिया, पर बंगाल का दरवाज़ा अख़बर पर खोल दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a detailed map-like vista of eastern India from Agra to the Bay of Bengal, with routes and rivers hinted through terrain, no markings
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view shows the Indo-Gangetic plain fading into the swampy, river-laced lands of Bengal and Orissa, with tiny processions and river craft dotting the landscape.

dialogue.text: For half a century, Afghan rulers of Bengal guarded the eastern marches—rich, humid, and far from Delhi’s gaze—until Akbar’s empire grew restless at its edge.

i18n.hi: आधे सौ साल तक, बंगाल के अफ़ग़ान शासक पूरब की इन नम, धनवान और दिल्ली से दूर सरहदों की रखवाली करते रहे—जब तक अख़बर की सल्तनत को इन किनारों की बेचैनी न खटकने लगी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Munim Khan in his later years, seated in a Mughal court tent, low-angle to suggest authority yet age
panels.action: Munim Khan sits on a cushioned seat inside a Mughal campaign tent, beard streaked with white, eyes tired but sharp, courtiers and officers half-visible behind him.

dialogue.text: Akbar chose Munim Khan, an old companion of his youth and veteran of many fronts, as Khan-i-Khanan to tame Bengal’s frontier and test the limits of imperial reach.

i18n.hi: अख़बर ने अपने जवानी के साथी और कई मोर्चों के बूढ़े सिपहसालार मुनिम ख़ाँ को ख़ान‑ए‑ख़ानाँ बनाया—ताकि वह बंगाल की सरहद काबू करे और बादशाही पहुँच की हदें आज़माए।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Daud Khan Karrani in his prime, inside a Bengali-Afghan court, eye-level but tense
panels.action: Daud Khan Karrani stands in an ornate hall with Bengali arches and Afghan banners, youthful face hardened, one hand on his sword-hilt, Afghan chiefs clustered around him.

dialogue.text: Across the rivers, Daud Khan Karrani, last Afghan sultan of Bengal, held Gaur and the delta, guarding his father’s inheritance and the autonomy of the Afghan ashraf.

i18n.hi: नदियों के उस पार दाऊद ख़ाँ कर्रानी, बंगाल का आख़िरी अफ़ग़ान सुल्तान, गौर और डेल्टा थामे बैठा था—बाप की विरासत और अफ़ग़ान अशराफ की आज़ादी की रखवाली करता हुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot inside Akbar’s court in Fatehpur or Agra, slightly elevated, showing Akbar gesturing eastward toward Munim Khan in the assembly
panels.action: Within a grand Mughal hall, Akbar, barely in his thirties yet imperial in bearing, stands and gestures toward the east as Munim Khan bows before him among gathered nobles.

dialogue.speaker: Munim Khan and Daud Khan Karrani
dialogue.text: “The path to Bengal lies along the rivers, Padishah. We must go by water and by patience.”

i18n.hi: "बंगाल की राह नदी से जाती है, बादशाह। हमें पानी से चलना होगा, और सब्र से।"

panels.shot: epic riverine wide shot, low angle from water level showing long lines of Mughal warboats and supply craft moving downriver
panels.action: Rows of Mughal boats, some bearing cannons and soldiers, others laden with supplies, cut slowly down a broad river under monsoon-laden clouds, banners fluttering damply.

dialogue.text: Abu’l-Fazl writes that the imperial army moved like a floating city, slipping down the Ganga’s broad back, for Bengal could be reached more surely by water than by dust roads.

i18n.hi: अबुल‑फ़ज़्ल लिखता है कि शाही फ़ौज तैरते शहर की तरह थी, गंगा की चौड़ी पीठ पर फिसलती हुई—क्योंकि बंगाल तक पनघट की राह से पहुँचना धूल भरी सड़कों से ज़्यादा यक़ीनी था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Todar Mal conferring with Munim Khan on a riverbank camp, three-quarter view
panels.action: On a muddy riverbank, Munim Khan stands with the astute administrator Todar Mal beside rough maps spread on a low table, soldiers and tethered elephants in the hazy background.

dialogue.text: Todar Mal, master of revenue and roads, rode with Munim Khan, for conquest in Akbar’s age meant not only beating armies, but measuring fields and fixing taxes.

i18n.hi: तोडर मल, माल और रास्तों का उस्ताद, मुनिम ख़ाँ के साथ चला—क्योंकि अख़बर के ज़माने में फ़तह का मतलब सिर्फ़ फ़ौज तोड़ना नहीं, खेत नापना और लगान बाँधना भी था।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of Afghan cavalry mustering near a marshy plain, camera at horse height
panels.action: Afghan horsemen loyal to Daud Khan gather on a soggy plain edged with palm trees, their light cavalry lines forming as drums and war-cries stir the humid air.

dialogue.text: Daud answered by mustering Afghan horse and archers near Tukaroi, the low fields around Bajhaura turning into a chosen ground where Mughal order would meet Afghan memory.

i18n.hi: जवाब में दाऊद ने तुकड़ई के पास अफ़ग़ान घुड़सवार और तीरंदाज़ जुटा दिए—बझौरा के निचले खेत चुना हुआ मैदान बन गए, जहाँ मुग़ल निज़ाम अफ़ग़ान यादों से टकराने वाला था।

panels.shot: epic battle wide, slightly elevated, showing Mughal lines and Afghan forces facing across a broken, waterlogged field, no close combat
panels.action: On a broken field laced with pools and embankments, Mughal ranks with matchlocks and elephants hold steady lines while Afghan contingents mass opposite, banners snapping in a hot wind.

dialogue.text: On 3 March 1575, near Tukaroi and Bajhaura, the armies met. Mughal chronicles speak of firm ranks and Afghan valor; Afghan voices are lost, but the clash shook the frontier.

i18n.hi: ३ मार्च १५७५ को, तुकड़ई और बझौरा के पास लश्कर भिड़े। मुग़ल तवारीख़ पक्की क़तारें और अफ़ग़ान बहादुरी लिखती हैं; अफ़ग़ान आवाज़ें गुम हैं, पर टक्कर ने सरहद हिला दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Munim Khan on an elephant amid dust, slightly low angle, conveying strain and command
panels.action: Munim Khan, perched atop a caparisoned elephant, leans forward, hand raised in command, his face lined with exertion as dust and smoke blur the horizon around him.

dialogue.text: The Akbarnama exults that Munim Khan’s steadiness broke Daud’s lines, yet even Abu’l-Fazl admits the Afghan fight was fierce, the field uncertain until the hours wore on.

i18n.hi: अकबरनामा फख्र से कहता है कि मुनिम ख़ाँ की अडिगी ने दाऊद की लकीरें तोड़ दीं, पर अबुल‑फ़ज़्ल भी मानता है कि अफ़ग़ान लड़ाई सख़्त थी, मैदान देर तक अधर में लटका रहा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Daud Khan Karrani withdrawing with a small entourage through reeds and water channels, three-quarter rear view
panels.action: Daud Khan, armor dulled by spray and mud, guides his horse along a narrow causeway flanked by reeds, a few loyal chiefs riding close as they leave the field behind.

dialogue.speaker: Munim Khan and Daud Khan Karrani
dialogue.text: “To lose one field is not to lose a kingdom,”

i18n.hi: "एक मैदान हारने से kingdom नहीं जाता।"

panels.shot: intimate medium shot in a dim Mughal command tent, Munim Khan seated across from Daud’s envoys, table between them
panels.action: Inside a lamplit tent, Munim Khan sits upright as Afghan envoys in simple yet dignified dress stand across a low table, their faces wary, a sealed document resting between them.

dialogue.text: Victory did not end in slaughter. At Katak, near Cuttack, negotiations followed. The treaty spared Daud’s life and left him Orissa—on condition he yielded Bengal and Bihar.

i18n.hi: फ़तह कत्लेआम पर नहीं ख़त्म हुई। कटक के पास कटक में सुलह हुई। समझौते ने दाऊद की जान बख़्शी और उरीसा उसके हवाले छोड़ा—बदले में बंगाल और बिहार छोड़ने की शर्त पर।

panels.shot: two-shot of Munim Khan and Daud Khan Karrani meeting formally, side view, with distance between them
panels.action: Munim Khan and Daud Khan stand facing each other in an open pavilion, separated by a respectful distance, each flanked by their officers, a sense of wary calculation between them.

dialogue.speaker: Munim Khan and Daud Khan Karrani
dialogue.text: “Hold Orissa in peace, Daud. Bengal must now answer to Akbar.”

i18n.hi: "उरीसा अमन से रख, दाऊद। बंगाल अब अख़बर को जवाब देगा।"

panels.shot: wide shot of Gaur or a major Bengal city with Mughal standards being raised over its gates, seen from slightly low angle
panels.action: Mughal soldiers stand atop massive brick ramparts as imperial standards are hoisted above the city gate, townspeople watching from the streets below and from shaded balconies.

dialogue.text: By this treaty, Gaur and Bengal’s heartland passed into Mughal hands. Abu’l-Fazl celebrates that Bengal and Bihar became subahs, provinces, in Akbar’s imperial design.

i18n.hi: इस समझौते से गौर और बंगाल का दिल मुग़लों के हाथ आया। अबुल‑फ़ज़्ल लिखता है कि बंगाल और बिहार अब अख़बर की सल्तनत के सूबे बन गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Munim Khan in an improvised court at Tanda or a Bengal headquarters, receiving petitions, slightly high angle to show his weariness
panels.action: Munim Khan sits in a modest hall in Bengal, hearing petitioners and conferring with officers, his shoulders drooping slightly at the weight of new governance in a humid, unfamiliar land.

dialogue.text: Yet the conquest was fragile. Munim Khan, tasked with turning victory into order, struggled with distance, disease, and local chieftains who bowed slowly, if at all.

i18n.hi: पर यह फ़तह नाज़ुक थी। मुनिम ख़ाँ पर ज़िम्मा था कि जीत को निज़ाम में बदले, पर दूरी, बीमारी और धीरे‑धीरे झुकने वाले सरदारों से वह जूझता रहा।

panels.shot: somber medium close-up of Munim Khan on his sickbed in a Bengal riverside city, interior, side-lighting
panels.action: Munim Khan lies propped on cushions in a shaded chamber, face gaunt, attendants and a concerned physician nearby, while outside a hazy glimpse of river and palms shows Bengal’s landscape.

dialogue.text: In 1575–76, the old general’s strength failed. Nizamuddin Ahmad notes Munim Khan’s death in Bengal; with him, the first layer of Mughal authority there suddenly thinned.

i18n.hi: १५७५–७६ में बूढ़े सिपहसालार की ताक़त चूक गई। निज़ामुद्दीन अहमद लिखता है कि मुनिम ख़ाँ की मौत बंगाल में हुई—और उनके साथ ही वहाँ मुग़ल हुकूमत की पहली परत अचानक हल्की पड़ गई।

panels.shot: dynamic medium shot of Daud Khan Karrani in Orissa, rallying Afghan chiefs, low angle to show renewed resolve
panels.action: Daud Khan stands beneath a carved Orissan gateway, gesturing forcefully as Afghan chiefs gather around him, their expressions fierce, the lush countryside rising behind them.

dialogue.text: With Munim gone, Daud moved again. The same chronicles that praised the Katak treaty now record his renewed war, for the Afghan sultan could not live as a quiet vassal.

i18n.hi: मुनिम के जाते ही दाऊद फिर हिल उठा। वही तवारीख़ जो कटक की सुलह की तारीफ़ करती थीं, अब उसकी नई जंग लिखती हैं—क्योंकि अफ़ग़ान सुल्तान चुपचाप जागीरदार बनकर जी नहीं सकता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Husain Quli Beg’s Mughal army advancing toward the hills near Rajmahal and the Ganga gorge, bird’s-eye view
panels.action: A large Mughal host under Husain Quli Beg winds along the foothills near Rajmahal, the Ganga cutting through nearby gorges as the army pushes toward the frontier forts.

dialogue.text: Akbar sent Khan-i-Jahan Husain Quli Beg. In 1576, his forces moved on Rajmahal and the Teliagarhi passes, where the river corridor narrowed and resistance could be pinned.

i18n.hi: अख़बर ने ख़ान‑ए‑जहाँ हुसैन कुली बेग को भेजा। १५७६ में उसकी फ़ौज राजमहल और तेलियाघाटी दर्रों की तरफ़ बढ़ी—जहाँ नदी की गलियारा संकरा होकर दुश्मन को जकड़ सकता था।

panels.shot: tense medium-wide shot of opposing lines near Rajmahal/Teliagarhi, with hills and riverbank visible, no hand-to-hand
panels.action: Mughal infantry and cavalry stand arrayed near the rising ground of Rajmahal, matchlockers poised, as Afghan horse form in scattered lines, the glinting river curling beside the field.

dialogue.text: The Tabaqat-i-Akbari records a hard fight near Rajmahal and Teliagarhi. This time there was no treaty path back for Daud; the struggle would decide Afghanistan’s hold on Bengal.

i18n.hi: तबाक़ात‑ए‑अकबरी राजमहल और तेलियाघाटी के पास सख़्त जंग लिखती है। इस बार दाऊद के लिए लौट कर सुलह की कोई राह न थी—यही लड़ाई तय करने वाली थी कि अफ़ग़ान हाथ बंगाल पर टिकते हैं या नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Daud Khan Karrani after defeat, hands bound but posture proud, flanked by Mughal soldiers
panels.action: Daud Khan stands with his hands tied in front, robe disheveled but head held high, as Mughal soldiers stand guard on either side with an air of formal restraint.

dialogue.text: By July 1576, the Afghan sultan was in Mughal hands. The chronicles state plainly: Daud was executed—his fall marking the end of the independent Karrani sultanate.

i18n.hi: जुलाई १५७६ तक अफ़ग़ान सुल्तान मुग़ल क़ब्ज़े में था। तवारीख़ साफ़ लिखती हैं: दाऊद को क़त्ल किया गया—उसका गिरना कर्रानी सल्तनत के आज़ाद ख़ात्मे की निशानी बना।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bengal’s river delta with scattered forts and villages, subtle, serene yet watchful atmosphere
panels.action: Across a vast delta, rivers shimmer around islands of settlement and small forts, smoke rising from villages, with no large army visible, only the quiet spread of habitations.

dialogue.text: Modern historians note that with Daud’s death, Bengal became a Mughal subah on paper—but men like Isa Khan and the Baro-Bhuiyans still held their own pockets of power for decades.

i18n.hi: आज के मुहक़्क़िक कहते हैं कि दाऊद की मौत के साथ बंगाल काग़ज़ पर मुग़ल सूबा बन गया—पर ईसा ख़ाँ और बारो‑भुइयाँ जैसे सरदार कई दशकों तक अपनी‑अपनी ताक़त सँभाले रहे।

panels.shot: reflective medium close-up of an aged chronicler’s hand writing by lamplight, with faint silhouettes of Munim and Daud imagined in smoke above
panels.action: By lamplight, a chronicler’s hand moves across a manuscript, while in the drifting smoke above, faint shapes of Munim Khan on his elephant and Daud Khan on horseback seem to arise.

dialogue.text: Tukaroi’s treaty did not end Bengal’s story; it opened it, showing that battles begin empires, but the choices made after the ink dries decide how long those empires truly endure.

i18n.hi: तुकड़ई की सुलह ने बंगाल की कहानी ख़त्म नहीं की, उसे खोल दिया—दिखाते हुए कि जंगें सल्तनतें शुरू करती हैं, पर स्याही सूखने के बाद लिए गए फ़ैसले बताते हैं कि वे कितने दिनों तक टिकेंगी।

title_i18n.hi: तुकड़ई से अख़बर की तरफ़ खुला बंगाल

subtitle_i18n.en: When the River Road to Bengal Opened
